== Biography ==
'''Ann “Annie” Glasgow''' was born about 1848 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was a daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], a farmer, and [[Unknown-540861|Margaret Unknown]].

In 1851, Ann was living with her family at house 34 in Lisnagaver, in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim. Her father, John Glasgow, was recorded as a 50-year-old farmer born in County Antrim.<ref>
'''1851 Census of Ireland''':<br/>
The National Archives of Ireland; residents of house 34 in Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim.<br/>
[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf Census image] — [https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/ Transcription] (accessed 17 April 2024).
</ref>

On 18 February 1875, Annie Glasgow married '''Francis Bellingham''' at Finvoy Parish Church, County Antrim, according to the rites of the Church of Ireland. Both were described as being of full age. Francis was a bachelor and farmer residing at Culmore in the parish of Rasharkin. Annie was a spinster residing in the parish of Rasharkin. Their fathers were recorded as Thomas Bellingham and John Glasgow, both farmers.<ref>
'''Civil marriage registration''': Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875; Ballymoney registration district; Group Registration ID 2857472; image path: marriage_returns\marriages_1875\11190\8100682.tif.
</ref>

The marriage witnesses were Thomas Bellingham and Mary Anne McCaughern.<ref name="marriage">
'''Civil marriage registration''': Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875; Ballymoney registration district; Group Registration ID 2857472.
</ref>

Mary Anne McCaughern may have been [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]. If so, her presence as a witness may indicate a connection between Annie’s family and that of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]. The identification is plausible but should not be treated as proven from the marriage record alone.
A marriage for Annie Glasgow and Bellingham was registered on 18 February 1875 in the Ballymoney district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 18 February 1875, Ballymoney district, M/1875/I1/263/1/46.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-867]] is assessed at 96% (proved). Ann’s 1851 Lisnagaver family placement and 1875 marriage naming John Glasgow, farmer as father provide two compatible stages of identity. The locality, age and named father strongly connect the bride to John’s household, despite unresolved age/death details for John himself.

Held citation and associated historical narrative address this selected father-child identity; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Compare the original 1851 Ann relationship with the 1875 bride’s residence.

Source basis already held: [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf 1851 Census of Ireland:  The National Archives of Ireland; residents of house 34 in Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim.  Census image (http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf) — Transcription (https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/) (accessed 17 April 2024).]; [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1371 Civil marriage registration: Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875; Ballymoney registration district; Group Registration ID 2857472; image path: marriage_returns\marriages_1875\11190\8100682.tif.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



Ann’s estimated birth year is uncertain. A birth about 1848 is consistent with her presence in the 1851 census and with her being recorded as “full age” when she married in 1875. The previously stated birth year of 1857 cannot be correct if she was the same Ann recorded in the 1851 household.

The names Ann and Annie were commonly used interchangeably in Irish records of this period.
